tone.target: saturated 80s hard-rock lead with bright upper mids and chant-like sustain
tone.profile: saturated 80s hard-rock lead with bright upper mids and chant-like sustain
tone.summary: A saturated signal chain utilizing a Boost/OD for initial grit, followed by the UK 45 or UK 50 amp model, paired with a Marshall-style cab and Chorus/Delay for big, sustained 80s lead sounds.
corrections: push from blues rock to harder 80s arena rock
add more saturation and upper-mid aggression
keep sustain but avoid fuzzy gating

rig.name: Whitesnake - Still Of The Night - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up hum and unwanted noise inherent in high-gain recording.
Provide initial grit and boost the signal into the high-gain amp section for added sustain.
blocks.gap: Using Boost instead of OD/Green OD to maintain clarity while adding necessary drive push.

alternatives.reason: Good alternative, but Boost offers a cleaner, more focused mid-range lift suitable for lead sustain.

blocks.purpose: Add the necessary thick saturation and aggressive upper-mid bite required for 80s arena rock.
blocks.gap: The 'Distortion' model is chosen over RAT/Muff to keep the tone focused on high-gain sustain rather than pure fuzz.

alternatives.reason: Suitable for psychedelic tones, but Distortion provides a more controlled, aggressive hard rock bite.

blocks.purpose: Simulate the hot British stack (Plexi/Marshall) required for big, aggressive 80s rock tones.

alternatives.reason: Also excellent, but UK 50 often provides a slightly more aggressive upper-mid punch suitable for the 'bite' requirement.

blocks.purpose: Provide the classic Marshall-style cabinet sound and necessary upper-mid punch.
Add the characteristic 'big arena' shimmer and sustain lift common in 80s rock leads.
blocks.gap: Chorus is used to enhance the big, sustained quality rather than a specific effect requirement.

alternatives.reason: Too subtle for the required 'big arena' sound.

blocks.purpose: Implement the required 'light delay' to add depth and sustain without sounding muddy.
Aggressively boost the upper mids and high frequencies to achieve 'bright upper-mid bite' and cut through a mix.
Add subtle space and 'big arena' ambience without losing the aggressive attack.
blocks.gap: Room reverb is preferred over Plate/Spring for a more natural, large-scale rock venue feel.

alternatives.reason: Can sound too artificial or metallic in this context.

improvements.summary: Improve cabinet realism to better capture the hot British stack's upper-mid aggression and sustain.

proposals.reason: Enhance the aggressive, bright upper-mids needed for 80s arena rock sustain.
